info.bio: Clint Patrick Black es un cantante, compositor, músico, actor y productor de música country estadounidense. Firmado con RCA Nashville en 1989, el álbum debut de Black, Killin' Time, produjo cuatro sencillos número uno consecutivos en las listas Billboard Hot Country Singles & Tracks de EE. UU.

scenes.name: Roots-rock de los ochenta y cow-punk
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Como en 1970 tras 1966, la new wave de 1976 va seguida de un revival del roots-rock, esta vez gradual y disfrazado: punks que desfiguran los estilos tradicionales (X, Dream Syndicate, Gun Club) y los «cow-punks» que tocan country ambientado entre inadaptados: Long Ryders, Jason & The Scorchers, Fetchin Bones, Lone Justice, Beat Farmers. El populismo de Los Lobos, Del Fuegos, Del-Lords y Walkabouts; en la Costa Oeste, los dementes Camper Van Beethoven, Donner Party, Catheads, Thin White Rope y los American Music Club de Mark Eitzel; en Texas, Wild Seeds, Poi Dog Pondering, Glass Eye; en los Grandes Lagos, BoDeans, Soul Asylum, Afghan Whigs, Shrimp Boat y los canadienses Cowboy Junkies. Nashville se renueva con los neotradicionalistas (George Strait, Randy Travis, Garth Brooks, Lyle Lovett, Steve Earle, Dwight Yoakam) y el surf instrumental vuelve con Shadowy Men On A Shadowy Planet.

podcast.title: Criticism of Urban Cowboy's Impact on Country Music (2003)
podcast.body: Black initially expressed reluctance to be involved in the *Urban Cowboy* Broadway musical in 2003, echoing sentiments from others in the country music industry who felt the movie "harmed" country music. He believed it made the genre "less pure" by introducing too many pop influences, even though he later softened his stance. "His argument was a lot like others in the country music industry who said that country music was somehow harmed by urban cowboy it made it less pure was the way that black put it."

podcast.title: Urban Cowboy Musical Reluctance
podcast.body: Clint Black was initially hesitant to contribute music to the "Urban Cowboy" musical because he felt the movie had made country music "less pure" and "too popular." He even suggested changing the musical's name to Aaron Latham, who declined. Black and Charlie Daniels eventually provided music for the show. "Black said, well, I do have some problems with it. You know, people think that Urban Cowboy changed country music, made it less pure."
